trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox; proto-IBM Pacific-facing (Palau-Kyushu); exclude Ryukyu/Nankai (lon<132) and Yap-like south of 8N
age_basis: midpoint of published spreading range; rifting ~55 Ma, spreading ~54 to 33/30 Ma (used 55-30)
citation_short: Deschamps & Lallemand 2002 JGR; Hilde & Lee 1984 Tectonophysics; Sdrolias & Müller 2006 G3
notes: Primary: Deschamps & Lallemand 2002 (rifting ~55 Ma; spreading 54-33/30 Ma). Conflict: Hilde & Lee 1984 give 58-33 Ma (two spreading phases); Sdrolias & Müller 2006 compile 55 to 30-33 Ma. Sasaki et al. 2014 argue cessation ~36 Ma. Used 55-30 Ma (Sdrolias compilation aligned with Deschamps end). WPB opened behind proto-IBM (Palau-Kyushu Ridge), not behind Ryukyu. FP risk: proto-IBM trench in Müller2019 is west of the modern Mariana trench; a present-day-only Mariana box would miss this interval. This box is wider/west-shifted for 55-30 Ma only.

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox; northern proto-IBM Pacific-facing; exclude Nankai (lon<138)
age_basis: same WPB spreading interval as Mariana row; northern proto-IBM may be sparsely sampled
citation_short: Deschamps & Lallemand 2002 JGR; Sdrolias & Müller 2006 G3
notes: WPB was a single basin behind the proto-IBM arc. Northern (Izu-Bonin latitude) trench samples at 55-30 Ma are few in Müller2019. Same age choice as West_Philippine_Basin_Mariana. FP: Nankai is Eurasia-Philippine Sea subduction and is excluded by lon_min=138.

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox; IBM south of ~24N (Parece Vela behind Mariana/West Mariana Ridge)
age_basis: initiation ~30 Ma; organized spreading by ~29-28 Ma (chron 10-9); cessation ~15 Ma
citation_short: Okino et al. 1998 Mar Geophys Res; Sdrolias et al. 2004 Tectonophysics; Mrozowski & Hayes 1979
notes: Sdrolias et al. 2004: arc rupture and rifting at ~30 Ma; spreading by chron 9o (28 Ma), possibly chron 10o (29 Ma); cessation ~15 Ma during SE Asia plate reorganisation. Okino et al. 1998: PVB spreading. Mrozowski & Hayes 1979: chrons 10-5D (~30-17 Ma). Maffione et al. 2022 (IODP U1438) argue true spreading nearer ~24-22 Ma after 30-24 Ma rifting; we treat rifting+spreading as E. Used 30-15 Ma.

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox; Izu-Bonin trench (Shikoku Basin behind Izu-Bonin); exclude Nankai lon<138
age_basis: midpoint of 30 Ma rifting vs 27-26 Ma organized spreading; cessation 15 Ma
citation_short: Okino et al. 1994; Chamot-Rooke et al. 1987 EPSL; Sdrolias et al. 2004 Tectonophysics
notes: Twin opening with Parece Vela. Sdrolias et al. 2004: rifting ~30 Ma, spreading by 29-28 Ma, ridges joined ~23 Ma, cessation ~15 Ma. Chamot-Rooke et al. 1987 / Okino et al. 1994 often quote 27-15 or 26-15 Ma for Shikoku spreading. Used 29-15. Conflict: Maffione et al. 2022 delay true spreading to ~24-22 Ma. FP: Nankai excluded.

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox; Mariana latitudes after Parece Vela cessation and before Mariana Trough rifting
age_basis: bracketed by PV cessation (~15 Ma) and Mariana Trough rifting (~7 Ma); not a dated 'neutral' event
citation_short: Okino et al. 1998; Martinez et al. 1995 JGR; Sdrolias & Müller 2006 G3
notes: Documented cessation of PV spreading at ~15 Ma and later resumption seaward in the Mariana Trough. Labelled N (no active back-arc) rather than C; no cordilleran shortening is claimed. Overlap at 15 and 7 Ma is resolved by preferring E.

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox; modern Mariana Trench only (exclude Yap ~138E and Izu-Bonin lat>=24)
age_basis: midpoint of rifting 8-6 Ma and spreading from ~6-5 Ma; used 7-0
citation_short: Hussong & Uyeda 1981 DSDP 60; Martinez et al. 1995 JGR; Yamazaki et al. 2003 G3; Stern et al. 2003
notes: Hussong & Uyeda 1981 (DSDP Leg 60): rifting latest Miocene ~6 Ma. Martinez et al. 1995 / Sdrolias & Müller 2006: resumed ~7 Ma. Yamazaki & Stern / Yamazaki et al. 2003: spreading at 18N from ~6 Ma. Stern et al. 2003/2004: rifting after ~10 Ma, spreading ~5 Ma. Conflict: Wikipedia/some reviews quote spreading 3-4 Ma. Used 7-0 (rifting+spreading as E). FP: Izu-Bonin excluded by lat_max=24; Yap excluded by lon_min=142.

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox; Izu-Bonin after Shikoku cessation; Sumisu rifts are not treated as a BAB
age_basis: Shikoku cessation ~15 Ma; no subsequent back-arc spreading behind Izu-Bonin
citation_short: Okino et al. 1994; Taylor 1992; Sdrolias & Müller 2006 G3
notes: After Shikoku cessation the Izu-Bonin arc has no organized back-arc basin. Sumisu/Torishima rifts are nascent (Pliocene-Quaternary) intra-arc rifts, not a spreading BAB; left as N with that caveat. FP: Nankai excluded by lon_min=139. Japan Trench is a separate segment (lat>=35).

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox wrap; Tonga Trench (lon 175 to -168); lat -26 to -14; not Kermadec
age_basis: opening ~6 Ma; spreading 6-5.5 Ma in the north, southward propagation
citation_short: Parson & Hawkins 1994; Taylor et al. 1996; Ruellan et al. 2003 G3; Hawkins 1995 ODP 135
notes: Ruellan et al. 2003 / Parson & Hawkins 1994: seafloor spreading started 6-5.5 Ma in northern Lau and propagated ~700 km south. Taylor et al. 1996 three-plate kinematics for Brunhes. Geosphere 2022 map: opening ~6 Ma by Tonga rollback. Used 6-0. lon_min>lon_max means wrap across 180. FP: North Fiji is a separate segment; Havre/Kermadec split at 26S.

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox wrap; Kermadec Trench; rifting (not a mature MOR for most of the trough)
age_basis: initial splitting ~5.5 Ma; southern Havre may be <2 Ma (conflict noted)
citation_short: Parson & Wright 1996; Caratori Tontini et al. 2019 Nature Geosci; Wysoczanski et al. 2019 NZJGG
notes: Caratori Tontini et al. 2019: proto-Colville-Kermadec split ~5.5 Ma; early spreading burst 5.5-5.0 to 3.0-2.5 Ma then disorganised rifting. Wysoczanski et al. 2019 Ar-Ar: southern Havre magmatism <2 Ma and coeval with TVZ. Conflict: south may be much younger than 5.5 Ma. Used 5.5-0 for the Kermadec upper plate as a whole (rifting counts as E). Not full MOR spreading. FP: Hikurangi (south of 40S / east of this box) not included.

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox; South Sandwich Trench; East Scotia Ridge back-arc (not West Scotia Ridge)
age_basis: midpoint of 15-17 Ma spreading underway (Larter) vs possible C6 ~20 Ma start; used 16-0
citation_short: Larter et al. 2003 G3; Eagles et al. 2005 JGR; Eagles & Jokat 2014
notes: Larter et al. 2003: anomalies to C5C, spreading underway by 15-17 Ma; possibly as early as C6 (~20 Ma). Eagles & Jokat 2014: ESR onset ~17 Ma, overlapping West Scotia Ridge until WSR extinction ~6 Ma (Eagles et al. 2005: WSR C8 ~26.5 Ma to C3A ~6 Ma). West Scotia is NOT assigned to this Sandwich-trench box. Used 16-0. In Müller2019 the Sandwich trench only appears after ~15 Ma, matching this onset. FP: southernmost Chile / South Shetland lie west of lon_min=-42.

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox; Andaman-Nicobar Trench; Central Andaman Basin spreading (highly oblique)
age_basis: Kamesh Raju/Curray 4 Ma spreading; Jha et al. 2021 revise to 5.9 Ma; used 4.0 (range 4-6)
citation_short: Kamesh Raju et al. 2004 EPSL; Curray 2005 JAES; Jha et al. 2021 Tectonophysics
notes: Kamesh Raju et al. 2004 / Curray 2005: continual spreading in the Central Andaman Basin from ~4 Ma. Jha et al. 2021 revise opening to chron C3An.1ny (5.894 Ma). Conflict: Morley & Alvey 2015 argue sedimentation is incompatible with continuous 4 Ma spreading (episodic or incipient); Curray 2015 reply defends spreading + episodic deposition. Earlier Curray et al. 1979 had ~11 Ma. Used 4-0 with 4-6 range. Spreading is highly oblique (leaky transform); SubMap geodetic UPS is SS not E — expected 0 Ma mismatch. FP: northern Sumatra if lat_min too low; kept lat_min=5.

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox; Ryukyu Trench; Okinawa Trough continental rifting (not MOR)
age_basis: Miki 1995 first phase 10-6 Ma; Sibuet et al. 1987 middle-late Miocene first rifting
citation_short: Sibuet et al. 1987 JGR; Letouzey & Kimura 1986; Miki 1995
notes: Continental back-arc rifting, not seafloor spreading (Arai et al. 2017: still rifting even in the south). Sibuet et al. 1987: first phase middle-late Miocene, ceased in Pliocene; second phase from ~2 Ma. Miki 1995: 10-6 Ma then ~1 Ma. Timing debated (Kimura 1996: 6-4 Ma). Used 10-6. Gap 6-2 Ma left unclassified (not forced to N). FP: Nankai/SW Japan excluded by lon_max=133.

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox; Ryukyu Trench; active Okinawa Trough rifting
age_basis: second rifting phase from Plio-Pleistocene boundary ~2 Ma
citation_short: Sibuet et al. 1987 JGR; Letouzey & Kimura 1986; Miki 1995
notes: Sibuet et al. 1987: second rifting phase started ~2 Ma at the Plio-Pleistocene boundary and continues. Miki 1995 places the second phase at ~1 Ma. Southern OT may have local oceanic crust since ~2 Ma (debated). Used 2-0. Rifting counts as E (no MOR required).

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox; Japan Trench (not Ryukyu, not Kuril); Japan Sea is the back-arc
age_basis: ODP 127/128 major opening 28-18 Ma; rifting from ~32 Ma; termination ~15-12 Ma; used 28-14
citation_short: Tamaki et al. 1992 ODP 127/128; Jolivet et al. 1994 JGR; Sato 1994 JGR
notes: Tamaki et al. 1992: Japan Sea extending 32-10 Ma, major opening with basin volcanism 28-18 Ma (Ar-Ar basement 24-17 Ma). Sato 1994: extension from 32 Ma, major rifting 25-20 Ma, opening terminated ~14 Ma. Jolivet et al. 1994: early-middle Miocene, stopped ~15-12 Ma. Used 28-14. SPARSITY: Müller2019 Japan Trench samples are almost absent before ~15 Ma, so this E interval is poorly sampled in the kinematics catalog. FP: Izu-Bonin split at 35N; Kurils east of 147E not included.

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox; Japan Trench; post-opening thermal sag / weak mixed stress
age_basis: Sato 1994: after ~14 Ma termination a neutral stress regime until ~4 Ma
citation_short: Sato 1994 JGR
notes: Sato 1994: after Japan Sea opening ended ~14 Ma, a neutral stress regime (weak extension and compression) prevailed until strong compression at ~4 Ma. Labelled N. Overlap at 14 Ma prefers E; at 4 Ma prefers C.

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox; Japan Trench; basin inversion / E-W compression of the NE Japan arc
age_basis: Sato 1994: strong compression from ~4 Ma; inversion of Miocene normal faults
citation_short: Sato 1994 JGR; Okamura et al. 1995
notes: Sato 1994: increase in westward Pacific motion ~4 Ma produced strong compression, reactivating Miocene normal faults (tectonic inversion). Some papers place localized inversion as young as ~1.8 Ma; 4 Ma is the regional stress-field change. This is arc/back-arc inversion, not Andean-style plateau building. SubMap Japan is mostly SS with some C.

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox; Hellenic Trench / Aegean (exclude Calabria lon<18.5); continental back-arc rifting, not MOR
age_basis: Ring et al. 2010 Aegean-wide extension from ~23 Ma; midpoint of 15 vs 35-45 Ma debate; used 23-0
citation_short: Ring et al. 2010 AREPS; Jolivet & Brun 2010; Le Pichon & Angelier 1979; Brun & Sokoutis 2010
notes: NOT a MOR. Conflict on onset: (1) Le Pichon & Angelier 1979 / Angelier ~13-15 Ma from basins; (2) Ring et al. 2010: Aegean-wide lithospheric extension from ~23-19 Ma (core complexes); (3) Jolivet & Brun 2010 / Brun & Sokoutis 2010: rollback-driven extension from ~45-35 Ma; (4) Lister/Gautier core complexes ~30 Ma; (5) some 2022 papers delay regional extension to ~15 Ma. Used 23-0 (Ring 2010) as a cited midpoint of the 15 vs 45 debate. Most extension after ~15 Ma (van Hinsbergen 2010; Brun 2016 acceleration). FP: Calabria excluded; Cyprus/Cyprean not included (lon_max=30.5).

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox; Calabrian Arc / Ionian subduction; Tyrrhenian back-arc
age_basis: major rifting from ~10 Ma (Tortonian); Vavilov spreading ~4 Ma; Marsili ~2 Ma
citation_short: Rosenbaum & Lister 2004 Tectonics; Kastens et al. 1988 GSA Bull; Malinverno & Ryan 1986
notes: Rosenbaum & Lister 2004: major Tyrrhenian rifting from ~10-9 Ma (Tortonian), two rollback episodes. Kastens et al. 1988 (ODP Leg 107): synrift Tortonian-Messinian on Sardinia margin; Vavilov basaltic crust before Marsili. Gueydan/Nature Comm 2022 compilation: Vavilov 4.3-2.6 Ma, Marsili ~2-1 Ma. Used 10-0 (rifting+spreading as E). Still opening (slow). FP: Hellenic excluded by lon_max=18.5; Apennine shortening is in the orogenic wedge, not this trench box.

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox; New Britain Trench; Manus/Bismarck back-arc
age_basis: Manus Spreading Centre <3.5 Ma (Taylor 1979); East Manus rifting <0.78 Ma
citation_short: Taylor 1979; Martinez & Taylor 1996 Mar Geophys Res; Taylor & Martinez 2003
notes: Taylor 1979: spreading on MSC/ETZ started <3.5 Ma. Martinez & Taylor 1996: Brunhes-age plate reorganisation; MSC wedge opening during Brunhes; East Manus distributed rifting. Some papers quote Bismarck opening from Finisterre collision ~3.7-3.0 Ma and spreading only in the last 0.78 Myr. Used 3.5-0 for the New Britain upper plate. FP: Solomons (~159E, -10) and Trobriand/Woodlark excluded. Older times in this box stay Unknown (pre-Manus).

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox; Vanuatu/New Hebrides Trench; North Fiji Basin back-arc
age_basis: rifting/opening from ~12 Ma after Vitiaz polarity reversal; still spreading
citation_short: Auzende et al. 1988, 1995; Pelletier et al. 1993; Martin 2013 Tectonophysics
notes: Auzende et al. 1988/1995: NFB opening from ~12 Ma in three stages (NE-SW 12-7, N-S 7-3, E-W since ~3 Ma) accompanying clockwise rotation of Vanuatu after Vitiaz lockup. Martin 2013: Fiji CCW rotation 10.2-1.56 Ma, Vanuatu CW from 12/10 Ma. Used 12-0. FP: Tonga is east of 175E / west of -168; this box is the east-dipping Vanuatu trench, not Tonga. D'Entrecasteaux collision locally compresses the central Vanuatu arc — a known along-strike exception not split out here.

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox; South America west coast, Altiplano-Puna latitudes (not Colombia, not Patagonia)
age_basis: shortening onset 50-45 Ma (range 60-40); continuous Cenozoic shortening to present; used 50-0
citation_short: Oncken et al. 2006 Andes book; Oncken et al. 2012 G3; Horton 2018 AREPS; Garzione et al. 2008 Science; Schellart 2024 ESR
notes: Oncken et al. 2006/2012: Central Andean shortening begins 45-50 Ma, rate increase ~32-27 Ma, deformation in the plateau until ~7 Ma then eastward into Subandes; still shortening. Horton 2018 / Barnes & Ehlers 2009: deformation and eastward migration from ~60-40 Ma. Incaic (late Eocene) and Quechua (Miocene) pulses are phases of one protracted Cenozoic shortening, not a switch to E. Garzione et al. 2008: paleoelevation rise is faster than shortening (delamination debate) — we classify UPS as C from shortening, not from uplift rate. Schellart 2024 ESR: Andes as the wide-slab shortening end-member vs Scotia extension. Used 50-0. Conflict: some authors put most growth after ~25 or ~15 Ma; onset still Paleogene. FP: Northern Andes (Colombia/Ecuador, lat> -12) and south-central Chile (lat< -32) excluded; Peru flat-slab is still shortening so C is appropriate if the box clips it.

trench_match_keywords_or_bbox: bbox; Cascadia Trench; no back-arc basin
age_basis: Juan de Fuca-Cascadia configuration in this catalog from ~30 Ma; no Cenozoic back-arc spreading
citation_short: Wells et al. 1998 Geology; Wells & McCaffrey 2013; Johnson et al. 2004 Tectonics
notes: NO back-arc. Labelled N not C: Cascadia is not an Andean cordilleran retroarc. Wells et al. 1998: Oregon forearc rotates clockwise; northward motion shortens western Washington against the Canadian Coast Mountains (margin-parallel N-S shortening, not trench-normal Andean C). Southern Cascadia has an extensional volcanic arc on the trailing edge of the rotating block (Basin and Range), which is NOT a Cascadia back-arc BAB. SubMap Geodetic_UPS for Cascadia is SS — agrees with N, not with C. Do not treat Washington fold-and-thrust (Yakima, Puget) as E vs C at the trench. Müller2019 Cascadia trench samples exist from ~30 Ma.
